Turns off the interrupts of the menu screen: white background, raster_split_enable and flash_enable off, the raster interrupt off, multicolour off.

Sets the size of a circle: the second point (shape_x1, shape_y1) follows the cursor, and $3b85 draws the band circle again at each move (a second draw removes it). Moves a circle: keeps shape_x0 - shape_x1 in delta_x and shape_y0 - shape_y1 in delta_y. Then the second point follows the cursor and the centre moves with it, in the limits 0-cursor_limit_x and 0-cursor_limit_y. $3b85 draws the band circle again at each move. delta_x = shape_x0 - shape_x1 (16 bits)
delta_y = shape_y0 - shape_y1 (16 bits)
shape_x0 = shape_x1 + delta_x

Line command (code 2). Shows the label LINE (script $2eb1) and the picture. The first press sets the start point, the second press sets the end point. Then the line moves with the cursor until the third press. Then the line is drawn with the brush in current_colour.
While the tool shows the line with XOR, current_colour is the background colour.

Moves the end of the line (line_x1, line_y1) with the cursor and shows the line with XOR ($2793) until a new button press. Keeps the last cursor position in shape_x0/shape_y0. A long press off the pad erases the line, restores current_colour from saved_colour and goes to tool_exit.
Removes the return address: tool_exit does not return.

Moves the line with the cursor until a new button press. The cursor sets the end (line_x1, line_y1). The start keeps its distance delta_x/delta_y from the end, in the limits 0-max_x and 0-max_y. Shows the line with XOR and erases it at the end. A long press off the pad goes to tool_exit.
delta_x = line_x0 - line_x1 (16 bits).
Negative: the start X is 0.
High byte not 0: the start X is max_x.

Waits for a button press while the pen is on the pad. Then sets both ends of the line (line_x0/y0, line_x1/y1) to the cursor and draws this point with XOR ($2793). A long press off the pad restores current_colour from saved_colour and goes to tool_exit. Line, Lines, Rays, Circle, Disc, Box, Frame and Copy use it.

Box command (code 7). Shows the label BOX. The first press sets a corner, the second press sets the other corner. Then the box moves with the cursor until the third press. Then fill_box fills the box in current_colour.

Frame command (code 4). Shows the label FRAME. The first press sets a corner, the second press sets the other corner. Then the frame moves with the cursor until the third press. Then brush_rect draws the frame with the brush in current_colour.

Moves the corner (shape_x1, shape_y1) with the cursor and shows the rectangle with XOR (xor_rect) until a new button press. Then erases the rectangle. A long press off the pad erases it, restores current_colour from saved_colour and goes to tool_exit. Box, Frame and Copy use it.

Moves the rectangle with the cursor until a new button press. The cursor sets the corner (shape_x1, shape_y1). The corner (shape_x0, shape_y0) keeps its distance delta_x/delta_y, in the limits 0-max_x and 0-max_y. Shows the rectangle with XOR and erases it at the end. A long press off the pad goes to tool_exit.
delta_x = shape_x0 - shape_x1 (16 bits).
High byte not 0: shape_x0 is max_x.

Fills the rectangle with the corners (shape_x0, shape_y0) and (shape_x1, shape_y1) in current_colour: draws one horizontal line ($2788) for each row, with the one-pixel brush at $1868. Puts the smaller coordinates in shape_x0/shape_y0. Restores brush_ptr at the end.
brush_ptr = $1868: the brush of one pixel.
Draws the rectangle with the corners (shape_x0, shape_y0) and (shape_x1, shape_y1) with XOR: plot_vector = $18c2, then draw_rect. A second call erases it.

Draws the rectangle with the corners (shape_x0, shape_y0) and (shape_x1, shape_y1) through plot_vector ($279e). When the corners are in one column or one row, draws one line. Else draws four lines: left side, bottom, right side, top. The 2nd, 3rd and 4th line start one pixel after their corner.
Draws the rectangle with the corners (shape_x0, shape_y0) and (shape_x1, shape_y1) with the brush: plot_vector = plot_brush, then draw_rect.

Fill command (code 9). Shows the label FILL. While the pen is on the pad, keeps the cursor position in shape_x0/shape_y0 and moves the cursor sprites there. On a button press with the pen on the pad, fills from the kept point ($3709). A long press off the pad goes to tool_exit.
Mirror mode: halves the cursor coordinates.

Draw command (code 1). Shows the label DRAW and waits for the button to go up. While the button is up, the start of the line follows the cursor. While the button is down, draws a line with the brush from the last point to the cursor ($2788), and the cursor becomes the last point. A move of 25 pixels or more on one axis changes the last point and draws nothing. A long press off the pad goes to tool_exit.
button_press_edge = button_held.
Unreachable bytes after the JMP: the instruction BEQ $1455.

Leaves a drawing tool. The callers jump here and remove their return address first. When mirror_mode_saved is set, sets mirror mode again (mirror_mode_on). Runs the script at $1dd3, then goes to the menu ($0b4a).
Runs the script at $1dfe. The script starts with op 9 to bitmap_mode_on. The tool start code at $0dd0 calls it.
Compares the ends of the line (line_x0, line_y0) and (line_x1, line_y1). C = 0 when they differ by less than 25 on both axes, else C = 1.
25 pixels.
Sets the end of the line (line_x1, line_y1) to the cursor (cursor_x, cursor_y).
Runs the script at $1e7c. The code of the Erase command ($0c24) calls it.
Shows the picture: sets bitmap mode ($d011 bit 5), multicolour mode ($d016 bit 4) and the bitmap at offset $2000 of the VIC bank ($d018 bit 3). Then sets the screen on ($0a42).
Shows the text screen: clears bitmap mode ($d011 bit 5), multicolour mode ($d016 bit 4) and $d018 bit 3. Then sets the screen on ($0a42).

Gives in A the pixel value (0-3) for current_colour in the cell of pixel_ptr. 0 = the background colour. Loads the cell colours (load_cell_colours), then continues at colour_slot_in_cell. Also an entry of the JMP table at $0900.

Gives in A the pixel value (1-3) of the cell colour (cell_colour_1-3) that is current_colour. When no cell colour is current_colour, counts the pixels of each value in the 8 bytes of the cell. The value with the fewest pixels (the higher value when equal) gets current_colour in the screen or colour RAM (write_cell_colours), and A gives this value.
work_ptr = first bitmap byte of the cell.

Sets cell_screen_ptr and cell_colour_ptr for the cell of the selected pixel (bitmap_row_base, pixel_x) and reads the cell colours into cell_colour_1-3 (read_cell_colours). Does nothing when the cell is the cell of the last load (cached_cell_ptr).
(bitmap_row_base - $6000) / 8 = row * 40.
+ pixel_x / 4: the column of the cell.
Screen at $5c00.
$5c + $7c = $d8: the page of colour RAM.

Reads the colours of the cell at cell_screen_ptr and cell_colour_ptr: cell_colour_1 = high nybble of the screen byte, cell_colour_2 = low nybble, cell_colour_3 = colour RAM. Then stores pixel_ptr AND $f8 in cached_cell_ptr.
Writes cell_colour_1 (high nybble) and cell_colour_2 (low nybble) to the screen byte at cell_screen_ptr, and cell_colour_3 to the colour RAM at cell_colour_ptr.
Mirror command (code $0d). Changes mirror mode on or off (toggle_mirror_mode), then goes back to the menu (return_to_menu).
Inverts bit 0 of mirror_mode and copies it to mirror_mode_saved. Then sets the drawing limits of the new mode (mirror_mode_on or mirror_mode_off).
Sets mirror_mode to 1 and the drawing limits to the upper left quarter of the picture: max_x = 79, max_y = 99.
Sets mirror_mode to 0 and the drawing limits to all of the picture: max_x = 159, max_y = 199. mirror_mode_saved does not change. Zoom and Copy call it.
Oops command (code $10). Runs the script at $1eb5, then goes back to the menu (return_to_menu).
Starts the raster interrupt ($0a9b), sets the screen on ($0a42) and goes to the menu ($0b63).

Xcolor command (code $0a). Shows the label XCOLOR. On a button press, reads the colour of the pixel under the cursor into target_colour and replaces it with current_colour in all of the picture. When target_colour is the background colour, the background colour ($d021, background_colour) becomes current_colour, and clear_colour_pixels runs for the old and for the new colour. Else each screen nybble and colour RAM value that is target_colour becomes current_colour. When current_colour is the background colour, clear_colour_pixels runs in place of the replacement. A long press off the pad goes to tool_exit.
Pixel value to colour.
Increments cell_screen_ptr and cell_colour_ptr. Z = 1 when cell_colour_ptr is $dbe8, after the last of the 1000 cells.
Sets cell_screen_ptr to $5c00 and cell_colour_ptr to $d800, the first cell.
For each of the 1000 cells: each pixel value (1-3) whose cell colour is target_colour gets its pixels set to 0, the background (clear_slot_pixels).
A = pixel value (1-3). In the 8 bitmap bytes of the cell of cell_screen_ptr ($6000 + 8 * cell number), sets each pixel with this value to 0.
work_ptr = (cell_screen_ptr AND $03ff) * 8 + $6000.
ASL and ADC #0 two times: rotates the byte left by 2 bits.

Plots the brush (brush_ptr) in current_colour around the selected pixel (pixel_x, pixel_y). The brush is a list of (dx, dy) byte pairs; $80 ends it. A point outside 0-max_x or 0-max_y is not plotted. In mirror mode each point is plotted 4 times ($1808), else one time ($1841). At the end selects the centre pixel again ($18f7) and gets its pixel value (get_colour_slot). It is a plot_vector routine of the line routines.
X > max_x: the point is not plotted.
Y > max_y: the point is not plotted.
Skips dy of a point that is not plotted.
Plots the dither pixel (plot_dither_pixel) at 4 points: (X, Y), (159 - X, Y), (159 - X, 199 - Y) and (X, 199 - Y). Input: X = x (0-159), Y = y (0-199). Keeps cursor_x and cursor_y.

Plots one pixel at X = x (0-159), Y = y (0-199) in the colour of the dither pattern: dither_colours[(y and 1) * 2 + (x and 1)]. $1525 gives the 2-bit value of that colour in the cell, plot_pixel_bits writes it. current_colour does not change.
Colour of this point of the dither pattern.
A = 2-bit value of current_colour in this cell.
Brush shapes. Each brush is a list of (dX, dY) offsets from the centre, signed bytes; $80 ends the list. The table at $0dc0 points to the 8 brushes. Brush 0: 1 point.
Brush 1: a block 2 pixels wide and 3 pixels high.
Brush 2: 2 points on a diagonal.
Brush 3: a diagonal line of 5 points.
Brush 4: 3 points on a diagonal, 3 pixels apart.
Brush 5: 6 points, 2 at the centre and 4 at the corners.
Brush 6: a vertical line of 6 points.
Brush 7: a horizontal line of 7 points.
Writes the 2-bit value in A into the pixel at pixel_ptr. Call set_pixel_address first. Jump table entry $0915.
Plot vector of the line routine $279e ($2793 puts it in $52/$53). In Mirror mode it inverts the pixel at 4 mirrored points ($281a), else at one point (invert_pixel).
Inverts both bits of the pixel at pixel_ptr (EOR %11). Call set_pixel_address first.
Shifts the 2-bit value in A to the position of the pixel (pixel_shift) and puts it in pixel_bits. Returns A = the byte at pixel_ptr, Y = 0.
Reads the pixel at X = x (0-159), Y = y (0-199). Returns A = its 2-bit value (0-3).
Returns A = the 2 bits of the pixel at position X (4 = left, 1 = right) of the byte in A.

Sets pixel_ptr, pixel_mask and pixel_shift for the pixel at X = x (0-159), Y = y (0-199) of the bitmap at $6000. It keeps the line address when Y is the same as before, and does nothing when X and Y are both the same. Returns X = pixel_shift.
Same pixel as before.
Start of the character row Y / 8.
Add the line in the row (Y and 7).
(X and $fc) * 2 = 8 bytes for each column of 4 pixels.
AND masks that clear pixel 0-3 of a multicolour byte.
Start address of each of the 25 character rows of the bitmap at $6000 ($140 bytes for each row).
Sets up the cursor sprites: offsets 18/25, X MSB off, sprites off, in front of the picture, hi-res. Runs cursor_sprites_script and brush_cursor_0 (the arrow), then cursor_on.
Lets the IRQ flash the cursor (cursor_colour_enable = 1), then cursor_sprites_on.
Sets cursor_sprite_mask to $cf (sprites 0-3, 6 and 7). read_cursor copies it to $d015 while the pad is touched.
Changes the colour of all 8 sprites between black and light grey. The IRQ calls it (by $0a25) while cursor_colour_enable is set.
Sets the colour of all 8 sprites to black.
Sets $d027-$d02e to A.
Hides the cursor: stops the flash, clears cursor_sprite_mask and turns all sprites off.
Reads the pad and converts it to screen units. No touch (pad Y $e6 or more, or both values below 10) gives cursor_x = $ff.

Reads the pad (sample_pad) and converts it to screen units (pad_to_screen) in cursor_x (0-$9f) and cursor_y (0-$c7). No touch (pad Y $e6 or more, or X and Y both below 10) gives cursor_x = $ff and sprites off; pad Y $e6 or more also sets pad_untouched and counts off_pad_count up to 16. A touch clears off_pad_count and turns on the sprites in cursor_sprite_mask. In Mirror mode it also keeps the position folded into the top left quarter in scratch_byte and mirror_cursor_y. Returns X = cursor_x, Y = cursor_y.
Stops the sound of voice 1 and clears pad_untouched.
Mirror mode: X >= 80 gives 159 - X.
Reads the cursor (read_cursor), then moves the cursor sprites to it (move_cursor_sprites).

Moves the cursor sprites to cursor_x, cursor_y. Sprites 0-5 are a block of 3 columns (24 pixels apart: 0/1, 2/3, 4/5) and 2 rows (21 lines apart); sprites 6 and 7 (the tool label) are 33 lines below sprite 0. Does nothing when cursor_x = $ff. In Mirror mode, cursor_x and cursor_y then get the folded position from read_cursor.
The label sprites go off the screen bottom.
Moves one sprite to screen X = A * 2 + 24 and Y = cursor_y + 50. Input: A = x (0-159), X = 2 * sprite number, Y = the bit of the sprite in $d010.
Script: sets the colour of all 8 sprites to black and the sprite pointers at $5ff8 to $60-$67 (sprite data $5800-$59ff). Then it continues into clear_cursor_script.
Script: clears the sprite data at $5800-$58ff (sprites 0-3), clears the label sprites with script $2e9f, and sets the destination to sprite 1 ($5840) for a brush cursor script.
Brush cursor scripts: each draws the mark of one brush into sprite 1 ($5840). Brush 0: an arrow that points up and left.
Brush 1 mark: a block 4 bits wide and 3 rows high.
Brush 2 mark: 2 points on a diagonal.
Brush 3 mark: a diagonal line.
Brush 4 mark: 3 points on a diagonal.
Brush 5 mark: 6 points, 2 at the centre and 4 at the corners.
Brush 6 mark: a vertical line of 6 rows (op 5 repeats one row).
Brush 7 mark: a horizontal line.
Addresses of the 8 brush cursor scripts. The brush code and $7f ($4f5a: 0, 2, ... 14) is the index ($0c11).
Calibration: screen X = (pad X - 20) * 4 / 5 (0-$9f), screen Y = pad Y - 20 (0-$c7).
Converts pad units to screen units: X = (pad X - 20) * 4 / 5 (0-$9f), Y = pad Y - 20 (0-$c7). Values out of range become the limit. Input and output: X, Y.
Puts A * 4 in temp_word/temp_word_hi (16 bits).
Divides the 16-bit value in temp_word/temp_word_hi by 5 (temp_word_hi must be below 5). Returns A = the quotient (8 bits); temp_word_hi keeps the remainder.

Sets the border black and blanks the screen ($d011 = $0b). With the character ROM visible, it runs menu_charset_script (charset at $5000). Then it selects screen $5c00 and charset $5000 ($d018 = $74) in VIC bank 1 ($dd00).

Repeats hit_test until hit_code is not 0. Then it subtracts the table bytes at hit_cell_ptr + Y - 2 and + Y - 4 from cursor_x and cursor_y, and returns A = hit_code. Only the jump table entry $0903 points to it; the runs did not execute it.
4 bytes that nothing executes. As code they are LDA $F0, BEQ $1C85.
Reads the pad (cursor_x, cursor_y), then looks up the cell under the cursor in the table at hit_table_ptr. hit_code gets the code of the cell, or 0.
Finds the cell under the cursor (hit_lookup), then moves the cursor sprites (move_cursor_sprites). hit_code gets the code of the cell, or 0.

Reads the cursor (read_cursor) and looks for the cell that holds cursor_x, cursor_y in the table at hit_table_ptr: count, then 5 bytes for each cell (Y max, Y min, X end, X min, code). hit_code gets the code of the first cell that matches, or 0. No table (hit_table_ptr = 0) gives 0.
Turns the 5 pad samples of each axis into one value (the median, from sort_samples). The cursor does not move when the samples spread by 5 or more.

Smooths the 5 pad samples of each axis (sort_samples) into cursor_x and cursor_y, in pad units. When a result differs from the raw value (pad_x_raw, pad_y_raw) by 5 or more, pad_spread gets the difference and cursor_x = cursor_y = 1. When both results are below 5, both become 0. Sets pad_read_enable. Jump table entry $0906.

Smooths the 5 pad samples of each axis (smooth_samples) into cursor_x and cursor_y, in pad units. When a result differs from the raw value (pad_x_raw, pad_y_raw) by 5 or more, pad_spread gets the difference and cursor_x = cursor_y = 1. When both results are below 5, both become 0. Sets pad_read_enable. Jump table entry $0906.
Sorts the 5 samples at $56-$5a. The middle one is the median.

Smooths the 5 samples in smooth_buffer. Each step puts (s[i] + 2 * s[i+1] + s[i+2]) / 4 into s[i]: 3 steps, then 1 step. The result in s[0] is the sum of the samples with the weights 1, 4, 6, 4, 1, divided by 16. It does not sort.
Adds A to sample_sum (16 bits).
Divides sample_sum by 4.
Draws the menu screen with the script at $3ee7.
A copy of the 8 bytes of draw_menu. Nothing executes or reads it.
Script: saves the colours of the picture before the menu uses the screen: screen RAM $5c00 to $c000, colour RAM $d800 to $c3e8, background ($e1) to $c7d0.
Script: copies 1000 bytes with all RAM visible. Destination and source come from the argument stack (op 14).
Script: copies 1000 bytes with I/O visible. Destination and source come from the argument stack.
Script: turns on the bitmap mode ($14ef) and puts the saved colours back: $c000 to $5c00, $c3e8 to $d800, $c7d0 to the background ($e1).
Start-up script: fills colour memory, then op 9 jumps to disk_protection.
Start-up script: sets the background of the picture ($c7d0) to 1 and copies it to $d7e8 and $dfe8 (RAM under the I/O). Then op 9 calls disk_protection.
Script: fills the screen colours at $c000 with $e8 and the colour RAM copy at $c3e8 with the pair $00, $0b (1000 bytes each).
Script at the start of the main program: clears the picture (new_picture_script), then copies the bitmap $6000 to $8000 and to $e000.
Script: SEI, then fills $0900-$477f with 0 (2 times 8000 bytes). The disk protection runs it ($3a8f).
Script: clears the colours (clear_colours_script) and fills the bitmap $6000-$7f3f with 0.
Script: fills 8000 bytes at the destination with 0.
Script: fills 1000 bytes with the fill byte. The destination comes from the argument stack.
Script: copies the picture to the undo buffer: bitmap $6000 to $8000, $c000 to $d000, $c3e8 to $d400, $c7d0 to $d7e8 (RAM under the I/O).
Script: copies the undo buffer back to the picture: $8000 to $6000, $d000 to $c000, $d400 to $c3e8, $d7e8 to $c7d0.
Script: copies the bitmap $6000 to $a000, then saves the colours (save_colours_script).
Script: copies the bitmap $a000 to $6000, then shows the picture with its saved colours (show_picture_script).
Script: copies 8000 bytes from the source to the destination with all RAM visible.
Script: copies the second character set of the character ROM ($d800, 2048 bytes) to $5000, then puts the menu graphics into characters $5e-$f1: frame lines, tool icons and colour cells.
Characters $62-$6a.
Characters $6c-$6d.
Characters $79-$80.
Characters $82-$91.
Characters $92-$b0.
Characters $b1-$cf.
Characters $d0-$e2.
Characters $e3-$f1.
Script: writes the colour bar into colour RAM at $db9c: 2 rows of 16 colours, 2 cells for each colour, in the order 0-8, 11, 9, 12, 10, 13, 15, 14.
Script: sets the border to grey ($0c) and the background to white, then continues into clear_menu_screen_script.
Script: fills the screen $5c00 with spaces (1000 bytes).
Script: fills 1000 bytes at the destination with the fill byte.

Script: draws the storage screen: character $81 on all of $5c00, colour 12, the title 'Picture List For', the command texts (Save, Get, Name & Save, Change Disk, Init Disk) and the 16 slots PIC A-P. It continues after $23ff to $2479.
End of the Storage screen script that starts at $23ac: the last letter of "Save", the button texts, the slot texts "PIC   Empty" and the slot letters A-H (left) and I-P (right).
Script: fills the 16 slot fields, the button fields and the message line with the fill value (spaces in the screen, colour 0 in the colour RAM). The caller sets the destination.
Script: copies the 15 bytes of the file name at dir_entry_buffer to the destination (the slot field).
Script: adds 32 to the source pointer. The runs do not read these 3 bytes.
Script: sets the destination to the field of a slot. Argument: the row of the slot (1-8) on the argument stack. script_condition not zero: left column, else right column (20 characters more).
Script: shows "Erase Disk? Type "Y" For Yes" on the message line.
Script: shows "Enter Disk Name:", clears 12 characters after it and draws the entry caret.
Script: writes "N0:", the 12 characters of the disk name and "," and the first 2 characters of the name (the ID) to disk_command.
Script: writes "S0:" and the 15 characters of the slot field at the destination to disk_command.
Script: writes 9 spaces after the slot letter of the slot field. The destination does not change.
Script: clears the name of the slot field and draws the entry caret at the first character of the name.
Script: moves the destination back, writes a space and draws the entry caret.
Script: writes the fill value (the typed character) and draws the entry caret after it.
Script: draws the caret ($81, $1e, $81) on the row below the destination.
Script: writes $81 on the row below the destination, over the middle of the caret.
Script: shows "Formatting Disk" on the message line.
Script: writes "Error" and 23 spaces to drive_message.
Script: copies the 28 bytes of drive_message to the message line.
Script: writes $81 at the mark position after each slot field and clears the message line.
Script: marks the slot and shows "Saving Picture".
Script: marks the slot and shows "Getting Picture".
Script: writes the mark character $1f after the slot field (15 characters after the destination).
Script: puts the mark character $3e (colour 0) at row 18, column 2 of the menu, and $81 (colour 6) at row 21. Row 18 is the first row of the plain colours.
Script: puts the mark character $3e (colour 0) at row 21, column 2 of the menu, and $81 (colour 6) at row 18. Row 21 is the first row of the dithered colours.
Script: takes 2 characters and 2 colours from the argument stack and writes them at rows 18 and 21, column 2, of the menu screen and of the colour RAM.
Script: writes the 2 next values of the argument stack at the destination and 120 bytes after it.
Script: writes the fill value at the destination and increments the destination.
Hit table of the main menu: a count, then 5 bytes for each cell: Y max, Y min, X end (exclusive), X min, code. Codes $01-$11 are the commands, $40-$5f the colours, $80-$8e the brushes.
Hit table of the Zoom screen: 19 cells. Code 2: Y $00-$2f, code 3: Y $30-$47 (X $00-$9e); code 1: Y $4c-$af, X $0c-$92; codes $40-$4f: the 16 colours at Y $b0-$c7. The zoom code at $305e uses it.
Draws a line from (line_x0,line_y0) to (line_x1,line_y1) with the brush: sets point_routine to $17ad, then draw_line.
Draws a line from (line_x0,line_y0) to (line_x1,line_y1) with inverted pixels: sets point_routine to $18c2 (XOR plot, with the mirror points when mirror_mode is set), then draw_line.

Draws a line from (line_x0,line_y0) to (line_x1,line_y1) with the routine at point_routine (Bresenham). A vertical or horizontal line plots both end points. Another line plots line_dx or line_dy points: not the end point. Keeps $3e-$41. Changes A, X, Y, cursor_x, cursor_y.
A line that is not vertical and not horizontal: keeps $3e-$41 on the stack and gets the distances and directions.
Gets $3e-$41 back from the stack and returns.
Plots the point (X,Y) with the routine at point_routine. $18f7 gives the bitmap address of the point.
This load has no effect: $18f7 loads A from Y first.
Inverts the pixel at (cursor_x,cursor_y) and at the 3 mirror points (159-x,y), (159-x,199-y) and (x,199-y). Keeps cursor_x and cursor_y.
Mirror point on X: 159 - x.
Mirror point on Y: 199 - y.
Inverts the pixel at (X,Y): gets the bitmap address ($18f7), then $18ca.
Horizontal line: sorts the X values, then plots each point from line_x0 to line_x1. Keeps line_x0 and line_x1.
Vertical line: sorts the Y values, then plots each point from line_y0 to line_y1. Keeps line_y0 and line_y1.
Line with line_dx > line_dy: line_two_dy = 2*dy, line_two_dx = -2*dx, line_error = 2*dy - dx. Plots line_dx points.
Step on Y. When line_fill_corners is set, it first plots the corner point (new X, old Y).
Line with line_dy >= line_dx: line_two_dx = 2*dx, line_two_dy = -2*dy, line_error = 2*dx - dy. Plots line_dy points.
Step on X. When line_fill_corners is set, it first plots the corner point (old X, new Y).

The Storage screen (command $0f, also Change Disk). Draws the screen (script $23ac), sends "I" to the drive, reads the directory and shows each file whose name starts with $81 "PIC " in the next slot. Then it runs the Storage loop. Returns after a long press off the pad.
Clears the colours of the sprites ($19e1).
Opens the directory: file name "$", secondary address $60, $f3d5 sends the name. storage_free_slot starts at 1.
KERNAL: sends LISTEN, the secondary address and the file name.
Makes the drive talk, then reads the disk name (the text between the first quotes, at most 12 characters) to row 1, column 22 of the screen.
Destination: the screen at row 1, column 22.
FNLEN is a counter here.
Next directory line: skips to its quote, compares the first 5 bytes of the name with pic_name_prefix and puts the 15 bytes of the name in dir_entry_buffer.
$bc counts the 5 bytes of the prefix.
FNADR is the index into pic_name_prefix here.
Slot number of this file.
End of the directory or a read error: $f642 closes the serial file.
KERNAL: closes the serial file.
KERNAL error 5: writes "Device Not Present" to drive_message.
KERNAL error 4: shows "File not found".
A = the KERNAL error code of a failed load or save (carry set): 4 and 5 have their own texts, other codes show "error".
No action: clears storage_action and the label sprites of the cursor.
Storage loop: a long press off the pad returns to the caller. A press on a cell runs the cell.
Hit test of the cursor; a press clears the marks and the message, then selects the action of the cell code.
Slot number 1-16.
A slot after the first empty slot becomes the first empty slot.
A slot: the slot number is at most storage_free_slot. Sets the destination to the slot field, then runs storage_action.
Init Disk: asks "Erase Disk?"; only "Y" continues. Then gets a disk name of 1-12 characters, sends "N0:name,id" and checks the drive status.
Empties the keyboard buffer.
The disk name has at most 12 characters.
Save: storage_action = 1 and the cursor label "save".
Get: storage_action = 2 and the cursor label "get".
Name & Save: storage_action = 3 and the cursor label "name".
Saves the picture to the slot. A slot that has a file: sends "S0:" and the old name first.
The slot has a file: build the scratch command with the old name.
The first empty slot: clears the name (not after Name & Save) and adds the slot.
Sets the file name from the slot field and saves the picture ($3351).
Gets the picture of the slot. The first empty slot does nothing.
Shows "Getting Picture", sets the file name from the slot field and loads the picture ($33a6).
The save and load routines jump here when the drive status is not 00 after the open: removes their return address and shows the error.
Shows drive_message on the message line.
Name & Save to the slot: gets a name of 1-8 characters, then saves. A slot that has a file: sends "S0:" and the old name first.
Sets the file of a picture: name = the 15 bytes at script_dst (the slot field: $81 "PIC ", the letter, a space and the name), logical file 5, device 8, secondary address 0.
15 characters: the name in the slot field.
Sends the command "I" (init_command) to the drive on channel 15. Also used by the disk protection ($3a85).
Shows "Formatting Disk" and sends the 18 bytes of disk_command ("N0:name,id") to the drive.
Sends the 18 bytes of disk_command to the drive on channel 15.
Opens the command channel with the name in A/X/Y, then closes file 15.
Opens file 15 on device 8, secondary address 15, with the name of length A at X/Y (SETNAM, SETLFS, OPEN). Also used by the disk protection ($3a62, $3a78).
Sets the destination to the field of the slot in hit_code.
Sets the destination (script_dst) to the field of slot A (1-16). Slots 1-8 are the left column, 9-16 the right column. Changes script_condition.
Slots 1-8: script_condition = slot (not zero) means the left column.
Clears the name of the slot field and gets a name of at most 8 characters. Carry set: no characters.
The picture name has at most 8 characters.
Text entry at the destination: at most entry_max_length characters $20-$5a, DEL removes one, RETURN ends. Carry set: no characters. The script code draws the characters and the caret.
DEL.
RETURN.
Reads the status of the drive on channel 15 ($3adf) into drive_message after the text "Error". Carry clear: status 00.
Reads bytes from the serial bus up to a zero byte. Z clear: the read ended with a status.
Reads bytes from the serial bus up to a quote. Z clear: the read ended with a status.
Reads a byte from the serial bus (ACPTR) to A. Y = STATUS, Z set when STATUS is 0.
Writes A at the destination (script_put_fill_value) and increments the destination.
Waits for a key: lets the IRQ scan the keyboard, waits for 10 empty GETIN results, then waits for a key and stops the keyboard scan. Returns the key in A.
The IRQ calls SCNKEY while keyboard_scan_enable is not zero.
Start of the name of a picture file: $81 "PIC ". The directory read takes only the files whose names start with these 5 bytes.
File name "$" of the directory.
Disk command "I" (initialize).
Hit table of the Storage screen: PIC A-P ($81-$90), Save $01, Get $02, Name & Save $03, Change Disk $04, Init Disk $05.
The X min of PIC P is $0c. The PIC H cell is before it in the table and covers X $0c-$42 of the same rows.
Script: shows "Disk Not Initialized" on the message line. The runs do not read it.
Script: writes "Device Not Present" to drive_message. Used by storage_device_absent, and by check_drive_status ($3b37) when the drive does not answer.
Script: shows "File not found" on the message line.
Script: shows "error" on the message line.
Script: cursor label "name".
Script: clears the label sprites, then cursor label "get ".
Script: clears the label sprites, then cursor label "save".
Script: copies 4 glyphs of the charset at $5000 to the label sprites ($5983, $5984, $5985, $59c3). Argument: the 4 glyph addresses on the argument stack.
Script: copies 2 more glyphs to the label sprite at $59c0 ($59c4, $59c5).
Script: clears the 2 label sprites at $5980-$59ff.
Script: copies the 8 bytes of a glyph (address on the argument stack) to a column of a sprite, one byte in each sprite row.
Script: cursor label "line".
Script: cursor label "lines".
Script: cursor label "rays".
Script: cursor label "frame".
Script: cursor label "circle".
Script: cursor label "xcolor".
Script: cursor label "disc".
Script: cursor label "draw".
Script: cursor label "fill".
Script: cursor label "box".
Script: cursor label "zoom".
Script: cursor label "copy".
Script: cursor label "swap".

Zoom: shows the picture with the zoom cursor (all 8 sprites) and waits for a press on the pad. The press selects the top row of the zoom window (the cursor row - 3, at most 16) and the addresses of the window in the bitmap, the screen colours and the colour RAM. A long press off the pad returns. The code continues at $303f.
Cursor sprite offsets of the zoom cursor: X +$16, Y +$31.
zoom_row = cursor_y / 8 ($3153).

Puts the addresses of the window row on the argument stack ($4f47-$4f4c: colour RAM, screen, bitmap, high byte first) and the bitmap and screen offsets on the CPU stack. Moves the cursor Y into the window.
Argument $4f4a/$4f49: the screen address $5c00 + row * 40 of the first preview row.
Argument $4f48/$4f47: the colour RAM address $d800 + row * 40.
script_flag = 0: the script copies the picture rows to the preview.
cursor_y becomes the Y in the preview: minus row * 8.

Zoom: the place is chosen. zoom_left and zoom_top get the cursor point in the preview. The script zoom_view_script builds the zoom screen, zoom_draw_view draws the magnified view, and the hit table at $2728 becomes active.
Script zoom_view_script ($322e) with the 6 arguments at $4f47-$4f4c.
Sprite 6 (the frame on the magnified view) is double size in X and Y.
hit_table_ptr = $2728: the hit table of the zoom screen.
Zoom main loop. No touch and a long press closes the zoom.
Hit test of the cursor on the zoom screen. Code 1: the magnified view, code 2: the preview, code 3: the rows under the preview, $40-$4f: the colour cells.
Clears button_press_edge before the hit test.
Code 3: the cursor is under the preview. cursor_y becomes $2f, the last row that the view can start at. Then as code 2.
Code 2: while the button is down, the view starts at the cursor point in the preview (zoom_left, zoom_top), and zoom_draw_view draws it again.

Code 1: sprite 6 frames the 4x4 block under the cursor. The cursor point becomes the picture point X = (cursor_x - 12) / 4 + zoom_left, Y = (cursor_y - 76) / 4 + zoom_top, and sprite 7 marks it in the preview. While the button is down, the brush plots that point and zoom_draw_view draws the view again.
Sprite 6 at the block (X register $0c: sprite 6, Y register $40: its X bit 8 mask).
Sprite 7 at the point in the preview.
Plots the current brush at the point.
Other cells: sprite 6 follows the cursor X. A press gives hit_code to COLORCHK, which selects the colour of the cell.

25 lines.

Script of the zoom start ($2f7b): it clears 384 bytes of sprite data at $5800, writes $00 to $d026 and builds the sprite shapes of the zoom cursor at $5800-$597f (sub-scripts $32c4, $32cd).

Keeps the cursor in the zoom limits: cursor_x at most $7e (when the pad is touched), cursor_y at most $af. X and Y are the cursor point.
8 column offsets of the brush marker, one for each pair of brushes (index current_brush / 2).

copy_width and copy_height of the rectangle.

Exchanges the picture with the second picture: blanks the screen, runs swap_script, sets the background colour, and shows the screen again.

Fill from the point (X, Y): changes all connected pixels of the colour of that point (target_colour) to current_colour, or to the dither colours. Uses a stack of 3-byte entries (direction, X, Y) from $c100. A press of the button stops the fill. Keeps brush_ptr, and sets dither_on to 0 at the end.

Fill from the point (X, Y): changes all connected pixels of the colour of that point (target_colour) to current_colour, or to the dither colours. Uses a stack of 3-byte entries (direction, X, Y) from $c100. A press of the button stops the fill. Keeps brush_ptr, and sets line_fill_corners to 0 at the end.
brush_ptr = $1868 during the fill.

A press stops the fill.
Stack pointer high byte $c0: the stack is empty.

When the pixel to the right is in the picture (X less than max_x) and has target_colour, pushes it with direction $80. Keeps cursor_x.
When the pixel to the left is in the picture and has target_colour, pushes it with direction $20. Keeps cursor_x.
When the pixel above is in the picture and has target_colour, pushes it with direction $40. Keeps cursor_y.
Pushes the pixels to the left and above (as fill_push_left and fill_push_up), then goes back to fill_loop.

Pushes the entry (A = direction, cursor_x, cursor_y) on the fill stack. With the stack pointer in page $ce, it first removes the entries of filled pixels (fill_compact_stack). From $cff0 on, it does not push.

Pushes one fill entry (direction temp_word, cursor_x, cursor_y) at point_x1/point_y1 + 3, and moves the fill stack pointer. A = the high byte of the pointer. When the stack is full ($cff0 or higher), it pushes nothing.

Pushes the entry, then copies each stack entry whose pixel does not have current_colour to the bottom of the stack ($c100 on). The stack pointer becomes the end of the kept entries. Keeps cursor_x and cursor_y.
Exchanges the stack pointer (point_x1/point_y1) with circle_dx/$45.
Copies the 3 bytes of the entry at the stack pointer to point_x0/point_y0, and moves point_x0/point_y0 3 bytes up.
When the pixel (cursor_x, cursor_y) has target_colour, gets its dither colour (when dither_on) and paints it with fill_set_pixel. Z is clear when the pixel has an other colour.
When the pixel (cursor_x, cursor_y) has target_colour, gets its dither colour (when line_fill_corners) and paints it with fill_set_pixel. Z is clear when the pixel has an other colour.

Paints the pixel at pixel_ptr with current_colour: bit pair 0 for the background colour, else the bit pair that $1531 gives for the cell. With Mirror on, paints the 4 mirrored pixels with fill_set_pixel_mirror. Z is set at the end.
Plots the pixel (X, Y) and its mirror images (159 - X, Y), (159 - X, 199 - Y) and (X, 199 - Y) with $1841. Keeps cursor_x and cursor_y.
Reads the pixel (cursor_x, cursor_y) and gives its colour in A. When dither_on, current_colour becomes the dither colour of that point. Z is set when the colour is target_colour.
Reads the pixel (cursor_x, cursor_y) and gives its colour in A. When line_fill_corners, current_colour becomes the dither colour of that point. Z is set when the colour is target_colour.
A = a bit pair 0-3 of a multicolour pixel. Gives its colour in A: background_colour, cell_colour1, cell_colour2 or cell_colour3 (the colours of the cell that $15b7 read).

Disk protection (switch PROTECTION): a RAM test at $8413, then two U1 block reads of track 1 sectors 1 and 2. TBC removed the checks after the reads. The routine resets the stack and jumps to start_main.

Disk protection (switch PROTECTION), reached from op 9 of startup_script. A RAM test at $8413: when the byte does not keep $01 and $00, protection_failed. Then for track 1 sectors 1 and 2: opens the buffer channel 5, sends a U1 command on channel 15 and reads the first digit of the drive status (protection_result). RAM test: $8413 must keep $01, then $00.
Command U1:5,0,1,1 (11 bytes): reads track 1 sector 1 into the buffer of channel 5.
NOPs of TBC over the check of the command.
NOPs of TBC over the check of the drive status.
Command U1:5,0,1,2: reads track 1 sector 2.
NOPs of TBC over the check of the command.
NOPs of TBC over the check of the drive status.
Sends I (initialize) to the drive.
Protection failed: the script at $1e71 does SEI and writes 0 to 16000 bytes from $0900. The program erases itself.
Protection: the name # of the buffer channel, and the two U1 commands that read track 1 sectors 1 and 2 into it.
Opens file 5 on device 8 with secondary address 5 and the name # (a buffer in the drive).
Reads the drive status from channel 15 up to the CR. Gives the first digit of the error number (and 15) in A and in protection_result.

Reads the status of drive 8 from channel 15 (TALK, TKSA $6f). The bytes up to the second comma go to drive_status_text: the error number, a space for the first comma, and the message. Then it skips the rest up to the CR. C is clear when the number is 00; then SA is restored. When no device answers (STATUS not 0 after TALK), the script at $2e0a writes DEVICE NOT PRESENT at $c7d1, and C is set.
script_flag = 0: no comma yet. The text index 0 goes on the stack.

The error number 00: no error.

Exchanges the point shape_x0/shape_y0 with shape_x1/shape_y1, so that the circle code uses the second point as the centre. The radius is the distance of the points in X plus the distance in Y, at most max_y. point_x0 and circle_dy get the radius, circle_dx gets 0.
Swaps the two shape points, so that the centre is the second point. The radius is |dx| + |dy| of the points, at most max_y. Sets point_x0 and line_dx to the radius.
Draws the circle of shape_x0/y0 and shape_x1/y1 with the XOR plot ($18c2): the rubber circle of the Circle and Disc tools. Keeps the shape points and the circle points ($3e-$41).
circle_step_vector = $3d49: plots 4 points at each step.
Draws the circle of shape_x0/y0 and shape_x1/y1 with the brush ($17ad).
Draws the disc of shape_x0/y0 and shape_x1/y1 with the brush: circle_step_vector = $3cde, which draws 2 lines at each step.

Steps through a quarter of the circle with the midpoint method: circle_dy starts at the radius, circle_dx at 0, the error (point_x1/point_y1) at 2 - 2 * radius. It calls the routine of circle_step_vector for each point. That routine ends the loop when circle_dy is 0.
Circle loop: chooses the next step from the sign of circle_error.
Error 0: diagonal step.
Error < 0.
Error < 0: t = 2 * error + 2 * circle_y_offset - 1 (in cursor_x/cursor_y). t <= 0: horizontal step, else diagonal step.
cursor_x/cursor_y hold the 16-bit value t.
Horizontal step: circle_x_offset + 1, plot, error + 2 * circle_x_offset + 1.
Diagonal step: circle_x_offset + 1, circle_y_offset - 1, plot, error + 2 * circle_x_offset - 2 * circle_y_offset + 2.
Vertical step: circle_y_offset - 1, plot, error - 2 * circle_y_offset + 1.
Error > 0: t = 2 * error - 2 * circle_x_offset - 1. t <= 0: diagonal step, else vertical step.
Writes 2 * circle_error to cursor_x/cursor_y (a 16-bit work value).
Decrements the 16-bit value in cursor_x/cursor_y. Output: A = the high byte (cursor_y), with the N and Z flags of it.
Jumps through circle_plot_vector. The plot routine ends the circle (it drops the return address of circle_plot) when circle_y_offset is 0.

Plot routine of the disc: draws the row circle_y_down and the row circle_y_up from circle_x_right to circle_x_left with the span routine at $285b. It skips a row outside 0-draw_max_y. It keeps shape_x0, shape_y0 and shape_x1. When circle_y_offset is 0, it returns from the caller of circle_plot.
Clip X: $fe gives 0.
Skip the row when Y > draw_max_y (also $fe and $ff).
Span from shape_x0 to shape_x1 on row shape_y0.
Drop the return address of circle_plot: the circle is complete.
Clips a circle X coordinate. Input A: X, $fe (below 0) or $ff (above draw_max_x). Output A: 0 for $fe, draw_max_x for $ff, else X.

Plot routine of the circle outline: plots the four points (circle_x_right, circle_y_down), (circle_x_right, circle_y_up), (circle_x_left, circle_y_down) and (circle_x_left, circle_y_up) with plot_point_xy. It skips a point outside the drawing area. When circle_y_offset is 0, it returns from the caller of circle_plot.
Drop the return address of circle_plot: the circle is complete.

Calculates the four circle coordinates from the centre (shape_x0, shape_y0), circle_x_offset and circle_y_offset: circle_x_right/left = shape_x0 +/- 3/4 * circle_x_offset, circle_y_down/up = shape_y0 +/- circle_y_offset. A coordinate below 0 becomes $fe, a coordinate above draw_max_x or draw_max_y becomes $ff.
temp_word = 3 * circle_x_offset.
temp_word / 4.
circle_error = circle_error + 2 * circle_x_offset.
circle_error = circle_error - 2 * circle_y_offset.
circle_error = circle_error + 1.
Plots the current brush at X = X register, Y = Y register with the plot routine at $2811. cursor_x and cursor_y do not change.

Starts a short beep on SID voice 1: volume 14, pulse width $400, frequency $2ef0, attack 0, decay 3, sustain 0, release 0, triangle wave with the gate on. The IRQ calls it every 32 interrupts while off_pad_beep_on is not 0.

Test bit on and off: resets the oscillator.
Stops the beep: clears off_pad_beep_on, turns the gate of SID voice 1 off and sets the test bit. read_cursor calls it when the pad is touched.

Script interpreter: A/Y is the address of a script. Each opcode byte selects a routine in script_ops. Opcode $ff ends the script, or returns from a script call. An opcode with bit 7 set takes its operands from the argument stack in place of the script.
Jump table entry: read_bitmap_byte.
Jump table entry: read_cell_colour.
Saves A/Y in script_ptr and clears the loop stack, the return stack and the argument stack.
Reads the next opcode. $ff: end or return. Else run the opcode routine.
Opcode $ff: return to the calling script when script_return_stack has an entry, else end.
Gets one operand in A: pops it from script_arg_stack when script_stack_mode is not 0, else reads the next script byte.
Reads the byte at script_ptr in A and increments script_ptr. Y = 0.
Pops the top byte of script_arg_stack in A. Y = the new script_arg_index.
Runs the routine of opcode A: bit 7 goes to script_stack_mode, bits 0-6 select the entry of script_ops. The opcode routine returns to the interpreter loop with RTS.
Jumps to the address in temp_word. Op 9 also comes here.
Op 0 (lo, hi): sets script_src_ptr.
Op 1 (lo, hi): sets script_dest_ptr.

Op 2 (n, n bytes): copies the n bytes that follow in the script to script_dest_ptr and adds n to script_dest_ptr. script_src_ptr is then the end of the bytes. With bit 7: n and the bytes come from script_arg_stack.
Source = the bytes in the script.
Skip the bytes in the script.
Copies Y bytes from script_src_ptr to script_dest_ptr, last byte first.
Adds the count on the stack (0 = 256) to script_src_ptr and script_dest_ptr.
Op 2 with bit 7: pops n bytes to script_dest_ptr, first pop first, and adds n to script_dest_ptr.
Op 37 (n): copies n bytes from script_src_ptr to script_dest_ptr with all RAM (no ROM, no I/O) and adds n to both pointers.
Op 3 (n): copies n bytes from script_src_ptr to script_dest_ptr and adds n to both pointers.
Copies Y bytes (A = Y = count, 0 = 256) from script_src_ptr to script_dest_ptr and adds the count to both pointers.
Op 4 (n): swaps n bytes between script_src_ptr and script_dest_ptr with all RAM (no ROM, no I/O) and adds n to both pointers.

Op 5 (count, lo, hi): loop. The first time, it pushes an entry on script_loop_stack and jumps to the address. Each next time, it decrements the count and jumps again until the count is 0. Then it pops the entry and continues after the operands. Thus the code between the address and the op runs count + 1 times. With bit 7: the count comes from script_arg_stack. With a full loop stack, it continues after the operands.
Is this op 5 the top entry of the loop stack?
Skips the operands: 3 bytes, or 2 bytes with bit 7.
Pushes address lo, address hi, count, script_ptr lo and hi, then jumps to the address.
Pulls the new script_ptr (hi, then lo) from the CPU stack.
Op 6: SEI (disables the interrupts).
Op 7: CLI (enables the interrupts).
Op 8 (lo, hi): calls the script at the address. It pushes script_ptr on script_return_stack; opcode $ff of the called script returns.
Op 9 (lo, hi): jumps to the machine code at the address. The RTS of that code returns to the interpreter loop.
Op 10 (n): adds n (0 = 256) to script_src_ptr.
Op 11 (n): adds n (0 = 256) to script_dest_ptr.
Op 12 (n): writes script_fill_byte to n bytes at script_dest_ptr and adds n to script_dest_ptr.
Op 13 (byte): sets script_fill_byte.

Op 14 (n, n bytes): pushes the n bytes that follow in the script on script_arg_stack. The first byte is on top, so the next pops give the bytes in script order. The operands always come from the script.
Op 15 (n): adds n to script_arg_index. The n bytes above the top become stack bytes again. The operand always comes from the script.
Op 16: empties script_arg_stack.
Op 17 (n): removes n bytes from script_arg_stack. The operand always comes from the script.
Op 18: does nothing.
Op 19 (a, b, c): writes a to current_colour and script_op19_byte1, b to script_op19_byte2, c to script_op19_byte3.
Op 19 (a, b, c): writes a to current_colour and count_pixels_1, b to count_pixels_2 and c to count_pixels_3.
Op 20: calls $0915 (X = shape_x0, Y = shape_y0) and $0918 of the jump table at $0900, then adds script_step_x to shape_x0 and script_step_y to shape_y0.
Calls $0918, then adds the steps to shape_x0 and shape_y0.
Op 21 (x): sets shape_x0.
Op 22 (y): sets shape_y0.
Op 23 (dx): sets script_step_x.
Op 24 (dy): sets script_step_y.

Op 26 (a): calls $0918 with A = a, X = shape_x0, Y = shape_y0, then adds script_step_x to shape_x0 and script_step_y to shape_y0.
Op 27: pushes script_src_ptr on script_arg_stack (lo on top), for a later op with bit 7.
Op 28: pushes script_dest_ptr on script_arg_stack (lo on top), for a later op with bit 7.
Op 29: pushes shape_x0 on script_arg_stack.
Op 30: pushes shape_y0 on script_arg_stack.
Op 31: reads the byte at script_src_ptr into pixel_value and adds 1 to script_src_ptr.
Op 32 (n): adds n to shape_y0.
Op 33, and a subroutine: SEI, then $01 bits 0-1 = 0 (all RAM: no BASIC, no KERNAL, no I/O).
Op 34, and a subroutine: $01 bits 0-1 = 1 (BASIC, KERNAL and I/O on), then CLI.
Op 35 (lo, hi): jumps to the script at the address when script_condition is not 0.
Op 36 (n): subtracts n from script_dest_ptr.
Adds 2 to script_arg_index. Output X = the new script_arg_index.
Adds 1 to script_arg_index. Output X = the new script_arg_index.
Adds A to script_src_ptr. A = 0 adds 256.
